case_name: M. Sai Santoshi vs K.Madhava Rao
facts_of_case: The petitioner-wife has filed a case for dissolution of marriage under the Hindu Marriage Act, while the opposite party-husband has filed a case for restitution of conjugal rights in another court. The petitioner seeks to transfer the latter case to her own court.

legal_principles.principle: A party seeking transfer of a case has to demonstrate inconvenience and hardship in continuing the proceedings at the existing venue.
legal_principles.held: The burden lies on the petitioner-wife to establish that it is becoming inconvenient for her to participate in the proceeding at Berhampur.

legal_principles.principle: A party cannot be forced to travel long distances for the purpose of participating in court proceedings.
legal_principles.held: It is becoming inconvenient on her to part to participate in the proceeding at Berhampur.

outcome.final_order: Notice issued to the opposite party both in main case and interlocutory application by Registered Post with A.D. fixing a short returnable date.

use_for_drafting: drafting a petition for transfer of divorce proceedings
advising on residency and inconvenience in family court cases
assisting with drafting a response to a petition for restitution of conjugal rights
